newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger says shareholder launches suit.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger says shareholder launches suit.

text.p: Hollinger Inc said on Tuesday one of its shareholders has applied to lead a class action suit against the global publishing company in opposition to the proposed increase of preferred stock in connection with Hollinger's failed takeover attempt of Southam Inc.

Hollinger said one individual who owns shares of Class A common stock and Series B convertible preferred stock of Hollinger is seeking to be certified to lead the lawsuit, which seeks injunctive and monetary relief based on alleged violations of law requiring a class vote before a proposed increase in authorized preferred stock.
Hollinger said it is reviewing the complaint, which names Hollinger and its directors as defendants, and will respond accordingly.
The issuance of shares to Southam shareholders tendered their shares to Hollinger's C$23.50 per share takeover bid is set to be voted on at a special meeting of Hollinger shareholders on July 21.

Hollinger's offer involved C$13.50 in cash and a US$10 non-voting special share in Hollinger Canadian, a unit of Hollinger International Inc. Conversion privileges for the special share kick in after six months.

Hollinger said the complaint alleges violations of the provision of the Delaware General Corporation law requiring a class vote of the company's preferred stock in connection with a proposed increase of the total authorized preferred stock and alleged breaches by Hollinger and its directors of their fiduciary duties in connection with the July meeting and in connection with "certain intercompany stock exchanges described in the proxy statement."
